correctness.rationale: For \(\lambda\ge3\), properness makes the colour sets on the two shores disjoint. The first forcing move therefore implies that one opposite shore already displays exactly \(\lambda-1\) colours. That forces the other shore to the single missing colour; because one colour cannot then force back across when \(\lambda-1\ge2\), the first shore must have been total initially. This gives an if-and-only-if classification of non-total forcing assignments. Counting those assignments and then adding the remaining total proper colourings yields the formula. Direct enumeration independently confirmed the classification and formula for 18 small profiles.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact closed form for every complete bipartite graph throughout the previously nontrivial regime \(\lambda\ge3\), where the primary source has only examples and general hardness. Complete bipartite graphs are a canonical test family for graph-colouring invariants, and the result exposes a reusable structural mechanism: after the first force, one shore becomes monochromatic and cannot force back. The formula also resolves the printed \(K_{1,2}\) discrepancy as a consequence rather than as an isolated correction.
